fields.title: A Unified Machine Learning Framework and Efficient Pattern Mining for Dynamic Price prediction in E-Commerce
fields.co_authors: Ashwin K., Priyadharshini R., Rajeshwari L.
fields.publisher: Dr. Mahalingam College of Engineering and Technology
fields.abstract:
Dynamic pricing is essential for modern e-commerce platforms, allowing retailers to adjust product prices in response to market fluctuations, consumer preferences, competitor actions, and seasonal variations. Developing a comprehensive dynamic pricing system involves integrating multiple computational components, such as scalable data extraction, time-series preprocessing, pattern discovery, predictive modeling, elasticity analysis, and reinforcement learning-based decision-making.
This paper introduces a unified framework that merges machine learning, pattern mining, and reinforcement learning to enable real-time dynamic pricing in e-commerce settings. The system features: (i) an automated Selenium-based pipeline for daily price scraping, (ii) a reliable ETL workflow with data normalization and SQLite time-series storage, (iii) pattern detection based on volatility and change-point methods for analyzing product behavior, (iv) a CatBoost regression model tailored by category for forecasting next-day prices, (v) a hybrid elasticity estimation module employing simulated Bayesian priors to assess demand sensitivity, and (vi) a Thompson Sampling multi-armed bandit algorithm for selecting optimal prices under uncertainty.
Conducted experiments on a dataset of 1,246 products tracked over multiple days demonstrate forecasting errors ranging from 1.56% to 8.70% MAPE across categories, with the reinforcement learning agent showing effective revenue-focused convergence. Results confirm that combining elasticity insights with reinforcement learning enhances pricing strategy performance compared to static or purely machine learning approaches. The proposed architecture provides a scalable, production-ready solution for dynamic pricing in real-world online retail applications.
fields.keywords: Dynamic pricing, machine learning, time-series forecasting, pattern mining, change-point detection, price elasticity, reinforcement learning, multi-armed bandits, Thompson Sampling, CatBoost, e-commerce analytics

fields.title: Hybrid Federated Learning for Edge Intelligence in 6G Networks
fields.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid federated learning framework designed for bandwidth-constrained 6G edge environments. By combining local gradient compression with asynchronous server aggregation, the scheme achieves a 48% reduction in latency while maintaining 99.1% accuracy on decentralized computer vision tasks.
fields.keywords: Federated Learning, 6G Networks, Edge Intelligence, Gradient Compression

fields.title: Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Privacy-Preserving IoT Telemetry
fields.abstract: IoT devices emit sensitive sensory data that can expose operational secrets. We introduce ZK-Telemetry, a succinct non-interactive zero-knowledge proof system optimized for microcontrollers with under 256KB RAM, allowing sensor validation without revealing physical telemetry payloads.
fields.keywords: Zero-Knowledge Proofs, IoT Privacy, Cryptography, Microcontrollers

fields.title: Quantized Neural Networks for Real-time Malware Detection
fields.abstract: Endpoint security agents demand sub-millisecond execution without depleting battery life. This paper introduces 4-bit integer quantized Convolutional-Transformer architectures capable of inspecting binary opcodes in real-time with 0.02ms inference overhead.
fields.keywords: Quantized Neural Networks, Malware Detection, Cybersecurity, Model Optimization

fields.title: Advanced Packet Filtering in SDN Architectures
fields.abstract: Software-Defined Networks require ultra-low latency packet inspection engines. We demonstrate eBPF-accelerated flow tracking that reduces packet drop rates by 62% during terabit DDoS floods.
fields.keywords: SDN, Packet Filtering, eBPF, Network Security

fields.title: Edge-based AI for Forest Fire Detection
fields.abstract: Deploying thermal infrared camera nodes powered by solar panels across dense forest reserves allows early wildfire detection. Our tinyML algorithm detects thermal hotspots within 1.2 seconds of flame ignition.
fields.keywords: Edge AI, Wildfire Detection, TinyML, Thermal Sensors

fields.title: Blockchain Interoperability Standards
fields.abstract: Cross-chain atomic swaps often suffer from locking deadlocks and high gas overheads. This research formulates a lightweight decentralized relayer network protocol using state-verification proofs.

fields.title: Optimizing Transformer Models for Embedded Edge Vision Systems
fields.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViT) are notoriously compute-heavy. By introducing dynamic patch pruning and depthwise separable self-attention, we achieve 45 FPS on Raspberry Pi 5 edge devices.
fields.keywords: Vision Transformer, Edge Computing, Patch Pruning, Embedded AI

fields.title: Lightweight Cryptographic Protocols for Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) Networks
fields.journal: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
fields.abstract: Autonomous vehicles need sub-10ms signature verification for collision avoidance messages. We design an elliptic curve signcryption scheme resilient against impersonation and replay attacks.
fields.keywords: V2X, Elliptic Curve, Automotive Security, Signcryption

fields.title: Autonomous Anomaly Detection in Cloud Microservice Swarms
fields.abstract: Analyzing distributed OpenTelemetry traces across thousands of Kubernetes pods is challenging. We leverage Graph Neural Networks (GNN) to pinpoint root-cause service failures automatically.
fields.keywords: Cloud Computing, Graph Neural Networks, Microservices, Kubernetes

fields.name: Guest Lecture on augmented reality and virtual reality
fields.description: Augmented Reality (AR) adds digital objects and information to the real-world environment, while Virtual Reality (VR) creates a completely computer-generated environment. AR can be experienced through smartphones and smart glasses, whereas VR usually requires a headset. Both technologies are widely used in gaming, education, healthcare, training, shopping, and entertainment. They make experiences more interactive, immersive, and realistic.
